run.question:
Alertmanager alert KubePodNotReady (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-6c5c44cd44-47jmg since 2026-11-26T01:30:58Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The KubePodNotReady alert for otel-demo/frontend-6c5c44cd44-47jmg is explained by a misconfigured readiness probe added to the otel-demo/frontend Deployment at 2026-11-26T01:30:33Z. The new ReplicaSet frontend-6c5c44cd44 (revision 2) added readinessProbe httpGet path=/ready port=40, while the container declares only containerPort 8080 and its log shows Next.js serving on 8080. The kubelet therefore probes 10.244.2.18:40, nothing listens there, and 65 Warning Unhealthy events record 'connect: connection refused' between 01:30:34Z and 01:35:38Z, leaving the pod Ready=False (ContainersNotReady) with restartCount 0. The prior ReplicaSet frontend-5c847cc9bd (revision 1) had no readinessProbe, which is the only pod-template difference observed. The Deployment's managedFieldsSummary shows an Update by manager OpenAPI-Generator at exactly 01:30:33Z (generation 2, revision 2), coincident with the 'Scaled up replica set frontend-6c5c44cd44 from 0 to 1' event. The application itself shows no failure: the pod log shows a successful startup on 8080, frontend and frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counts were 0 in both a pre-rollout 20m window ending 01:30:00 and a post-rollout 5m window ending 01:36:00, and the frontend Service still had the older ready pod (10.244.2.176) as a ready endpoint while the new pod sat in notReadyAddresses. All other 26 otel-demo pods were Ready. The flagd-config ConfigMap has every flag at defaultVariant off, so flag-driven fault injection is not supported as the cause.

claims.text: Pod otel-demo/frontend-6c5c44cd44-47jmg (created 2026-11-26T01:30:33Z, owner ReplicaSet frontend-6c5c44cd44) has Ready=False and ContainersReady=False with reason ContainersNotReady and message 'containers with unready status: [frontend]'; its frontend container has ready=false, restartCount=0, started=true. Every other otel-demo pod returned in the same query had Ready=True.

A single Warning event group on pod frontend-6c5c44cd44-47jmg records 65 occurrences of reason Unhealthy, firstTimestamp 2026-11-26T01:30:34Z and lastTimestamp 2026-11-26T01:35:38Z, with message 'Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.2.18:40/ready": dial tcp 10.244.2.18:40: connect: connection refused'.

Deployment otel-demo/frontend defines for container frontend: containerPort 8080 named 'service', and readinessProbe httpGet path '/ready' port 40 scheme HTTP with failureThreshold 3, periodSeconds 5, timeoutSeconds 3; no livenessProbe and no startupProbe.

The two frontend ReplicaSets differ in exactly the probe setting: frontend-5c847cc9bd (revision 1, created 2026-11-26T01:23:02Z, readyReplicas 1) has readinessProbe null, while frontend-6c5c44cd44 (revision 2, created 2026-11-26T01:30:33Z, readyReplicas null) has readinessProbe httpGet path /ready port 40; both use the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-frontend and the same containerPort 8080.

Deployment otel-demo/frontend has generation 2 and annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2; its metadata.managedFieldsSummary lists helm Apply at 2026-11-26T01:23:02Z and an Update by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 2026-11-26T01:30:33Z (plus kube-controller-manager status update at the same time).

At 2026-11-26T01:30:33Z the frontend Deployment produced event 'Scaled up replica set frontend-6c5c44cd44 from 0 to 1', and pod frontend-6c5c44cd44-47jmg was Scheduled to kind-environment-worker at 01:30:33Z, container created 01:30:33Z and started 01:30:34Z.

The frontend container log of frontend-6c5c44cd44-47jmg shows a successful startup: '▲ Next.js 16.3.5', '- Local: http://frontend-6c5c44cd44-47jmg:8080', '- Network: http://frontend-6c5c44cd44-47jmg:8080', '✓ Ready in 0ms', '✓ Running next.config took 1.7ms'; no error lines, and no previous container instance exists.

Endpoints of Service frontend list address 10.244.2.176 (targetRef pod frontend-5c847cc9bd-dndlg) as ready and list 10.244.2.18 (targetRef pod frontend-6c5c44cd44-47jmg) under notReadyAddresses on port 8080.

Span-error metrics for the frontend services were zero in both a pre-rollout and a post-rollout window: increase over 20m ending 2026-11-26T01:30:00Z gave traces_span_metrics_calls_total STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 0 for service_name frontend and frontend-proxy (UNSET 13539.045 and 5981.632), and increase over 5m ending 01:36:00Z gave STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 0 for both (UNSET 16006.667 and 7020).

Sampled frontend spans in the window starting 2026-11-26T01:28:00Z show operations 'GET /api/data' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' with http.status_code 200 and 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, and none of the shown spans carry error_by_visible_tags=true.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (data key demo.flagd.json) has every flag at defaultVariant 'off', including failedReadinessProbe ('readiness probe failure for cart service'), imageSlowLoad ('slow loading images in the frontend'), cartFailure, paymentFailure and adFailure; the ConfigMap's only managed-field entry is helm Apply at 2026-11-26T01:23:02Z.

Rejected: the pod is failing because the container crashed, restarted or was OOMKilled. The container has restartCount 0, an empty lastState, started=true, and there is no previous container instance and no OOMKilled/Evicted evidence; the failure signal is repeated readiness-probe refusals, and the app log records a completed startup at 01:30:34Z.

Rejected: the pod is unschedulable or short of resources. The kubelet reported 'Successfully assigned otel-demo/frontend-6c5c44cd44-47jmg to kind-environment-worker' at 01:30:33Z and the container was created and started within one second; the pod phase is Running with PodScheduled=True.

Rejected: a flagd feature-flag fault injection (e.g. failedReadinessProbe or imageSlowLoad) caused the not-ready state. All flagd flags are at defaultVariant 'off' in the ConfigMap, failedReadinessProbe is described as a cart-service failure, and the observed failure is a kubelet TCP refusal on port 40, a port the container never declares.

The frontend Deployment is the only otel-demo Deployment carrying an httpGet readinessProbe besides otel-collector (which probes its own path '/' on port 13133); all other otel-demo Deployments declare no readinessProbe, so the port-40 probe is a frontend-specific setting.

The frontend Deployment PodTemplate change at 2026-11-26T01:30:33Z (readinessProbe added on port 40 instead of the container's declared 8080) is what makes the new pod permanently NotReady: nothing is listening on port 40, so the kubelet's /ready check is refused every 5 seconds and the pod never becomes Ready even though the application is running.

Verify whether port 40 is intended for the frontend readiness probe; for the running frontend container the probe should target the declared containerPort 8080 ('service'), on which the app logs show Next.js serving, so correcting the probe port (or removing the probe as in revision 1) would let the rollout complete.

gaps: Change history integration is not available, so no change record identifies who or what 'OpenAPI-Generator' is or why the probe was applied; only the managedFieldsSummary timestamp 2026-11-26T01:30:33Z and the ReplicaSet revision 1 vs 2 template diff link the change to the probe.

metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives only the last write per manager, not a field diff; the attribution of the port-40 readinessProbe to the 01:30:33Z OpenAPI-Generator Update is inferred from the revision 1/revision 2 template comparison, not from a recorded diff.

I could not exec into the pod or query the kubelet, so whether the frontend also answers /ready on 8080 is not directly observed; the probe never checks 8080, and the only 8080 evidence is the container log line.

The traces_search view for service frontend (2026-11-26T01:28:00Z-01:36:11Z) exceeded the token limit and was only read as a biased 60-row slice; spans after 01:30 are not fully observed, so no per-request failure rate is claimed.

A cluster-wide ConfigMap query filtering names on 'fault|chaos|inject|experiment' returned no objects; an empty result shows only that this query matched nothing and is not proof that no fault-injection object exists.
The alert's cluster label in the annotations is empty, so the alerting cluster identity was not verified from cluster objects.
next_steps: Compare the otel-demo/frontend Deployment spec against the Helm release values for the frontend readinessProbe to confirm whether port 40 came from an out-of-band patch by the OpenAPI-Generator client.
Identify the client identity 'OpenAPI-Generator' (API audit logs / who holds its credential) and review its patch payload at 2026-11-26T01:30:33Z.
After the probe is corrected, confirm the new ReplicaSet frontend-6c5c44cd44 pod becomes Ready and the Deployment rollout completes with readyReplicas 2.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

query.jq_expr: .items[] | select(.metadata.name|test("frontend")) | {name: .metadata.name, replicas: .status.replicas, ready: .status.readyReplicas, available: .status.availableReplicas, updated: .status.updatedReplicas, selector: .spec.selector, images: [.spec.template.spec.containers[] | {name, image, readinessProbe, env}], annotations: .metadata.annotations, generatedFrom: .metadata.ownerReferences}
